provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: The rule is D4-invariant: every frame (5x5 hollow square of original colour 1) gets a full-grid row and full-grid column through its bounding-box centre, painted with original colour 6 only on background (original 8) cells, so frame walls stay intact. Under any rotation/reflection, frames remain 5x5 squares, their centres map to the transformed centres, and a row+column cross maps to a column+row cross, so the emitted program works directly in visible coordinates without needing to pick an axis. Colour roles are specialized as constants: background = palette[8], frame = palette[1], line = palette[6]. Frames are found as 4-connected components of the frame colour (generator guarantees frames never touch), the centre is the bbox midpoint, and crossings between different frames' lines on background simply become the line colour.
draft_notes.limitations: Assumes the constructor's domain: only background and frame colours in inputs, frames are closed 5x5 rings that do not touch one another. If the frame colour were absent the program falls back to treating all non-background cells as frames. No tests were run.
